blocks.text: As it can be seen from the above explanations English tenses may be rendered in Russian by either the imperfective or the perfective aspect of the corresponding Russian verbs. However, the following hints may be helpful:

head: English
Russian
rows: 2. Present Perfect Progressive: I have been writing all morning.
Present, imperfective: Я пишу уже всё утро. («уже» usually added)
3. Any progressive tense: I am writing a letter. I was writing a letter. I will be writing a letter.
Imperfective aspect of the corresponding verb: Я пишу письмо. Я писал письмо. Я буду писать письмо.

items: Я с трудом могу загрузить песни на мой айпод.
I'm having a hard time downloading songs to my iPod.
The chief is speaking to me.
Я иду в поход с Томом.
Озеро Чад продолжает уменьшаться в размерах.
Lake Chad is continuing to shrink.
The notebook is lying on the table.

exercises.q: Я с трудом ___ (мочь) загрузить песни на мой айпод.
exercises.prompt: I'm having a hard time downloading songs to my iPod.

exercises.why: **говорить → говорит** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
exercises.prompt: The chief is speaking to me.

exercises.why: **жить → живёт** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ет belongs to the first (е) conjugation.
**делать → делают** — present tense, 3rd person plural: ending -ют belongs to the first (е) conjugation.
**сидеть → сидит** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
**продолжать → продолжает** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ет belongs to the first (е) conjugation.
exercises.prompt: Lake Chad is continuing to shrink.

exercises.why: **лежать → лежит** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
exercises.prompt: The notebook is lying on the table.

exercises.why: **ходить → ходит** — present tense, 3rd person singular: ending -ит belongs to the second (и) conjugation.
